page: Amazon Web Services m8id.xlarge is a general-purpose, eighth-generation cloud instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, allocating 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The host supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for int8 and tile matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, featuring 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) clocked at 7 GHz, alongside 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Local high-speed persistence is bundled via a dedicated 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network connectivity provides 2 Gbps of throughput without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the system contains no dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance. Single-core tests in Geekbench recorded a score of 2052.0, placing in the top quartile alongside strong outcomes in single-threaded gzip compression (34.06 GB/sec), bzip3 decompression (14.46 GB/sec), and text processing (2780.0). In contrast, total parallel compute capacity is constrained by the 4-vCPU envelope, with multi-core stress-ng tests yielding 4318.27 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 28.9 GB/sec, placing in the lower benchmark quartiles. Uncached large-block DDR5 memory bandwidth registers 44.5 GB/sec for reads and 31.41 GB/sec for writes.

For workload execution, the integrated NVMe storage and balanced memory facilitate microservices, low-latency caching, static web hosting (benchmarking at 8.7 GB/sec), and Redis caching reaching 7.34 million SET operations per second. However, heavier compute pipelines, PassMark database operations (2230.3), and larger language model inference show clear scale limitations, with 7B model generation dropping to 5.03 tokens/sec. The instance serves cost-effective general-purpose tasks requiring direct NVMe ephemeral scratch space without necessitating oversized memory or GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 16.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and bundled storage consisting of a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. The hardware incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions. Benchmark data reveals competitive single-core performance, scoring 2052.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside strong single-threaded compression and text processing throughput. Symmetrical multi-threaded throughput and complex database operations are limited by its 4-vCPU size. Supported by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the m8id.xlarge offers an efficient hardware envelope for standard web serving, Redis caching, microservices, and general-purpose workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
